_meta.description: Forward-tuning overrides for manager_pitching='v2', active for any sim date >= 2026-04-14 via should_use_forward_tuning(). Each key below has its own provenance block. See Syndicate/mlb_sim_accuracy_assessment_and_optimization_plan.md Phase 1 item #1 for full context.

starter_hook_add_pitches.description: Re-fit of the starter-hook-add-pitches override for the MLB manager_pitching='v2' model, made necessary by promoting log5/odds-ratio combination for hr_tgt/inplay_hit in sim_engine/pitch_model.py (2026-07-19) -- that change shifted the raw pitch-count bias curve enough that the prior fit (-11, from 2026-07-17 against the naive-average combiner) no longer lands near zero. Re-swept manually against the same 35-tune/11-holdout 2026-season backfill (seed 2026, 100 sims/game), grid [-12,-13,-14] under the new log5 combiner, calibration disabled to see the raw effect. See the log5 combiner promotion note in pitch_model.py's _combined().
starter_hook_add_pitches.rationale: Clean, monotonic bracket: -12 -> holdout bias +0.73 (tune), -13 -> holdout bias +0.44 / essentially zero on tune (-0.02), -14 -> overshoots negative (tune -0.73). -13 lands closest to zero on both tune and holdout without overshooting, and is a materially better pitch-count fit than the prior -11 value ever achieved even under the old naive-average combiner (holdout bias was +1.35 at best).

previous_fit.context: Fit against the naive-average rate combiner (pre-log5). Grid [-14,-11,-8,-5,-2]. Superseded by this entry once log5 combination was promoted for hr/inplay_hit.

starter_hook_stamina_excess_weight.description: New tunable added 2026-07-20: sim_engine/simulate.py's _starter_effective_hook previously hardcoded a 0.25 weight on stamina above the manager's baseline hook -- min(base,stamina) discarded any excess entirely, then only 25% of it was credited back, while below-baseline stamina got full credit via the min(). This severely dampened upside for high-stamina workhorses (a maxed-out stamina_pitches=115 vs base=95 only reached eff_hook=100, barely above a league-average pitcher's 92), which combined with a real data-attribution bug in _derive_stamina_pitches_from_season_stats (season-total pitches divided by start count alone, corrupting estimates for mixed-role pitchers -- see build_roster.py fix same day) to make pitcher pitch-count projections converge toward a narrow band regardless of real ace-vs-back-end differences. Fixed the data-attribution bug directly in code; made the 0.25 weight tunable and swept it here since it's a genuine magnitude question, not a correctness bug. Swept grid [0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00] against the same 35-tune/11-holdout 2026-season backfill, on top of the stamina fix + the newly-populated Statcast player-feature set (see data/statcast/features/) + selective log5 + starter_hook_add_pitches=-13.
starter_hook_stamina_excess_weight.rationale: Clean monotonic tune-day trend crossing zero near weight=1.00 (0.25->-0.63, 0.50->-0.38, 0.75->-0.15, 1.00->+0.06), but holdout generalization favored 0.75 over 1.00 (holdout bias +0.20 vs +0.39, outs_mae 3.877 vs 3.914) -- the tune-day optimum didn't hold on holdout, so the more conservative value was selected. HR/hits/total-runs metrics stayed completely flat across the whole grid (hr_avg_p 0.0945-0.0946, full_mae_total_runs 3.539-3.548), confirming this change is cleanly isolated to pitcher workload with no side effects.
